subject: psychology
title: Five Senses Adventure
welcome_lead: Sight, sound, smell, taste, touch — your five gates to the world. 👁️
meta_desc: Senses & Attention Adventure 1 — KS3 Psychology on the five senses.
final_note: You met the five senses and the body parts that pick up each one.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Each sense has a special organ:

  • Eye → light → brain.
  • Ear → sound waves → brain.
  • Nose → smell molecules → brain.
  • Tongue → taste buds → brain.
  • Skin → pressure and heat → brain.

Scientists now say humans have more:

  • Balance — inner ear.
  • Body position (proprioception).
  • Pain.
  • Temperature.

Senses are how the brain knows the world. 🌍

mcqs.q: What did Bowlby mean by monotropy?
options: One primary attachment figure (usually the mother) is qualitatively different and most important.
A child can only ever form one attachment.

mcqs.q: How are phobias MAINTAINED according to Mowrer's two-process model?
options: Through classical conditioning continuing over time.
Through operant conditioning - avoidance reduces anxiety (negative reinforcement).

mcqs.q: Why is high IQ a problem for the statistical infrequency definition?
options: Because high IQ is actually common.
It is statistically rare but not abnormal/undesirable.
